name: Murder at Blackwood Manor
plot: Private Investigator Arthur Pendelton is invited to an isolated mansion for a reading of a will, only to find himself trapped in a deadly game of cat-and-mouse when the relatives start dying one by one.

characters.name: Narrator
characters.description: An objective, slightly cynical narrator observing the events.

characters.name: Arthur Pendelton
characters.description: A seasoned, observant private investigator with a sharp mind.

characters.name: Lady Beatrice
characters.description: The wealthy, eccentric matriarch of the Blackwood family.

characters.name: Charles Blackwood
characters.description: The estranged, debt-ridden nephew eager for his inheritance.

characters.name: Evelyn
characters.description: The quiet, observant housemaid with a hidden past.

episodes.name: The Arrival
episodes.description: Arthur arrives at the storm-battered mansion just as the victims begin to fall.

episodes.name: The Locked Room
episodes.description: A body is discovered in a room locked from the inside.

episodes.name: The Killer Revealed
episodes.description: Arthur pieces together the clues to unmask the true culprit.

scenes.name: The Looming Storm
scenes.description: Arthur drives up to Blackwood Manor as a tempest brews.

scenes.name: Dinner with the Suspects
scenes.description: The family gathers for a tense dinner before the reading.

scenes.name: Investigating the Scene
scenes.description: Arthur examines the body and finds his first clue.

scenes.name: Interrogating Charles
scenes.description: Arthur confronts the nervous nephew in the study.

scenes.name: Evelyn's Secret
scenes.description: The housemaid reveals crucial information about the family's past.

scenes.name: The Second Murder
scenes.description: Another body is discovered, complicating the case.

scenes.name: Gathering the Clues
scenes.description: Arthur presents his grand theory to the surviving members.

scenes.name: The Confession
scenes.description: The killer attacks Arthur, leading to a final struggle.

dialogues.text: Thunder split the sky over Blackwood Manor, a vast estate perched upon the jagged cliffs of Cornwall.
A perfect night for a reading of a will. Or a murder.
Arthur Pendelton parked his vintage sedan and hurried through the pouring rain to the massive oak doors.
Mr. Pendelton? Come in, come in out of the storm. I am Evelyn, the housemaid.
Thank you, Evelyn. Rather dreadful weather for a family gathering, isn't it?
Lady Beatrice insisted the reading take place tonight, sir. Regardless of the storm.
I am curious, Evelyn. Why was a private investigator invited to the reading of Lord Reginald's will?
I... I do not know, sir. Lady Beatrice handles all affairs.
Inside the grand dining hall, the atmosphere was as chilly as the weather outside.
Ah, Mr. Pendelton. You finally arrived. I was beginning to think the storm had washed you out to sea.
It takes more than a bit of rain to wash me away, Lady Beatrice. My condolences on your husband's passing.
Save your platitudes, detective. We all know my husband was a loathsome man. I only invited you because someone has been sending me threatening letters.
Threatening letters? Oh, come now, Aunt Beatrice. You're just being paranoid in your old age.
Mind your tongue, Charles. The ink on your uncle's death certificate isn't even dry, and you're already sizing up the silverware.
I have significant debts, Aunt! The market has been unkind. I have a right to my inheritance!
Gentlemen, ladies, please. A threat is a serious matter. Do you have the letters, Lady Beatrice?
Locked in my safe. I will show them to you after dinner. Then, we will read the will.
The dinner passed in strained silence, punctuated only by the clinking of silver on china and the roaring thunder outside.
The soup was excellent, Evelyn.
Thank you, sir. Will there be anything else?
No, Evelyn. We will retire to the study. Except you, Charles. You smell of cheap gin.
You horrible old shrew! I hope Uncle left you nothing!
Charles stormed out of the dining room, slamming the door so hard the crystal chandeliers trembled.
Families. Such a disappointment. Come, Mr. Pendelton.
Just past midnight, Arthur was reviewing his notes in the guest bedroom when a piercing scream echoed through the corridors.
That came from the library!
Arthur grabbed his flashlight and his revolver, rushing down the dark, twisting hallways.
Mr. Pendelton! Mr. Pendelton!
Evelyn, what is it? Are you hurt?
It's... it's Lady Beatrice! I went to bring her a cup of tea, and...
Arthur pushed past the terrified maid and stepped into the library. The room was perfectly intact, except for the body of Lady Beatrice slumped over the mahogany desk.
Don't touch anything, Evelyn. Go wake Charles.
Arthur approached the body. A single silver letter opener protruded from the back of her neck.
Instantaneous. Professionally done. Whoever did this knew exactly where to strike.
He noticed a piece of ash on the desk near the fireplace. The threatening letters Lady Beatrice had mentioned were nowhere to be seen.
What is going on? Why is Evelyn crying hysterically in the hall?
Stay back, Charles. Your aunt is dead.
Dead? Oh, good god... I didn't mean it when I said those things at dinner! I swear!
Where were you for the past hour, Charles?
In my room! Drinking! I haven't left since dinner!
Can anyone corroborate that?
No! I was alone! Are you accusing me, Pendelton?
I am gathering facts. Fact one: You desperately need money. Fact two: Your aunt controlled the inheritance. Fact three: She was just murdered.
I didn't do it! I wouldn't even know how to stab someone like that! I'm a stockbroker, not an assassin!
Someone burned papers in the fireplace recently. The threatening letters she told me about.
Letters? I don't know anything about any letters.
Arthur thoroughly searched Lady Beatrice's room but found the safe empty.
Evelyn, a word, if you please.
Yes, sir?
You found the body. Was the door to the library locked when you arrived?
Yes. It's an old lock. It can only be turned from the inside, or with the master key. I have one, Lady Beatrice had the other.
And where is Lady Beatrice's key?
It... it usually hangs on her belt. But it isn't there now.
So the killer killed her, took her key, locked the door from the outside, and vanished.
It must be Charles. Everyone knows he hated her.
Too obvious, Evelyn. It's never the most obvious suspect. Tell me about Lord Reginald's previous staff.
They were all dismissed last month, abruptly. I was hired only two weeks ago from an agency in London.
Interesting. And did Lady Beatrice seem frightened of anything specific?
She mentioned a man from her past. Someone she thought was dead in the war.
The next morning, the storm had finally broken, but the telephone lines were dead.
The bridge is washed out. We are completely isolated until the authorities can arrive.
We're trapped in here with a murderer! I want to leave! I'll swim across the river!
Calm down, Charles. Panicking will only get you killed.
Mr. Pendelton! Come quickly! It's Charles!
What? Charles is right here with me.
No, I mean in the conservatory! There's another body!
They ran to the glass conservatory. Amidst the rare orchids lay the body of a man.
Wait... that's not me. But he's wearing my grandfather's signet ring!
Who is this man?
That's... that's Uncle Marcus. But he died in the war!
Apparently not. Does Lord Reginald have any other brothers?
Just Marcus. If he's alive... he inherits everything. Not me. Not Beatrice.
Lady Beatrice must have known he was alive. He was the one blackmailing her.
But who killed him? And who killed Lady Beatrice?
A very good question, Evelyn. Or should I say... Agatha?
I'm sorry, I don't follow.
Agatha Sterling. The illegitimate daughter of Marcus Blackwood. The agency in London doesn't employ an 'Evelyn'.
You? You're my cousin?
You're absurd, Mr. Pendelton.
Am I? You have a military tattoo on your wrist, poorly concealed by your maid's uniform. You strike with deadly precision. And you had the master key.
...They stole everything from my mother. Beatrice and Reginald. They left her in the slums to rot while they lived in this mansion.
So you killed my Aunt? And your own father?!
My father returned demanding his share, threatening to expose my existence. I couldn't let him take what was rightfully mine.
It's over, Agatha. Confess, and perhaps the courts will show mercy.
I don't need mercy, detective. I need you out of the way!
Agatha pulled a suppressed pistol from her apron and fired.
Get down, Charles!
Arthur dove behind a marble pillar as bullets shattered the glass windows behind him.
I've locked the mansion. I have enough fuel to burn this entire place to the ground with both of you inside!
You'll never escape the police. The river will strand you just as it has stranded us!
I have a boat hidden in the cove. Goodbye, Mr. Pendelton.
Arthur fired a blind warning shot, the loud crack echoing off the stone walls.
Drop the weapon! I won't ask again!
He stepped out from cover, his aim steady. Agatha hesitated, the hatred in her eyes conflicting with her instinct to survive.
Fine. Take me. But my mother is avenged.
She dropped the pistol, which clattered loudly against the floor.
Is it... is it over?
Yes, Charles. You can come out now. It seems you're the sole heir after all.
Let's find some rope. It's going to be a long wait for the police.
